title: Posterior prediction, credible sets, and Bayes actions

items.title: Posterior-predictive probability kernel
items.statement: For a supplied posterior probability kernel Π_y and future probability kernel Q_θ, define Q_y^pred(B)=∫Q_θ(B)Π_y(dθ); only globally supplied probability kernels are inputs.
items.strategy: Define the posterior-predictive mixture and make its proper-kernel input explicit.

references.title: Andrew Gelman et al., Bayesian Data Analysis, 3rd ed., §§1.3 and 2.5
Alicia A. Johnson, Miles Q. Ott, and Mine Dogucu, Bayes Rules!, Chapter 8 §§8.1 and 8.3

items.title: A posterior mixture of future kernels is a probability kernel
items.statement: The mixture Q_y^pred(B)=∫Q_θ(B)Π_y(dθ) is a probability kernel and integrates every nonnegative measurable future quantity by iterated integration.
items.strategy: Use the joint law of a prior and a probability kernel, then verify measurability in the observed-data coordinate.

references.title: Andrew Gelman et al., Bayesian Data Analysis, 3rd ed., §1.3
Alicia A. Johnson, Miles Q. Ott, and Mine Dogucu, Bayes Rules!, Chapter 8 §8.3

items.title: Posterior-predictive mean and variance decomposition
items.statement: If the posterior mixture has finite second moment, its mean is the posterior average of the future-kernel means and its variance is expected future variance plus posterior variance of the future mean.
items.strategy: Establish integrability from the second moment, pass first and second moments through the mixture, and expand the variance.

references.title: Andrew Gelman et al., Bayesian Data Analysis, 3rd ed., §2.5
Alicia A. Johnson, Miles Q. Ott, and Mine Dogucu, Bayes Rules!, Chapter 8 §8.3

items.title: Posterior credible set
items.statement: For α∈[0,1], a graph-measurable set-valued rule C(y) is a posterior credible set at level 1−α when Π_y(C(y))≥1−α.
items.strategy: Define posterior mass sets only for an already supplied posterior probability kernel.

references.title: Andrew Gelman et al., Bayesian Data Analysis, 3rd ed., §§1.3 and 2.5
Alicia A. Johnson, Miles Q. Ott, and Mine Dogucu, Bayes Rules!, Chapter 8 §8.1

items.title: Posterior quantiles are measurable and bracket their probability level
items.statement: For u∈(0,1), S_y={r∈Q:F_y(r)≥u} is nonempty and bounded below; q_u(y)=inf S_y is its real infimum, is measurable, and satisfies Π_y((−∞,q_u(y)))≤u≤Π_y((−∞,q_u(y)]).
items.strategy: Use kernel event measurability, countability and density of the rationals, the real infimum property, measure monotonicity, and continuity on monotone set sequences; prove the CDF bracket by contradiction without selecting sequences of rationals.

references.title: Andrew Gelman et al., Bayesian Data Analysis, 3rd ed., §2.5
Alicia A. Johnson, Miles Q. Ott, and Mine Dogucu, Bayes Rules!, Chapter 8 §8.1

items.title: Equal-tailed posterior quantile intervals are credible
items.statement: For a real-valued parameter and 0<α<1, the interval [q_{α/2}(y),q_{1−α/2}(y)] is graph-measurable and has posterior mass at least 1−α.
items.strategy: Prove the interval graph is measurable, then subtract the lower-tail bound from the upper-tail bound.

references.title: Andrew Gelman et al., Bayesian Data Analysis, 3rd ed., §2.5
Alicia A. Johnson, Miles Q. Ott, and Mine Dogucu, Bayes Rules!, Chapter 8 §8.1

items.title: Posterior median
items.statement: A median of a real posterior Π_y is an m satisfying Π_y((−∞,m])≥1/2 and Π_y([m,∞))≥1/2.
items.strategy: Use the two-sided half-mass inequalities, which allow nonunique medians.

references.title: Ryan Martin, Lecture Notes on Advanced Statistical Theory, §5.3.1, PDF pp. 104–105
Andrew Gelman et al., Bayesian Data Analysis, 3rd ed., §2.5

items.title: The lower posterior median is a measurable rule
items.statement: The lower quantile q_{1/2}(y) is a measurable posterior median for every real-valued posterior probability kernel.
items.strategy: Apply the quantile CDF bracket to the two defining median inequalities.

references.title: Ryan Martin, Lecture Notes on Advanced Statistical Theory, §5.3.1, PDF pp. 104–105
Alicia A. Johnson, Miles Q. Ott, and Mine Dogucu, Bayes Rules!, Chapter 8 §8.1

items.title: Finite posterior risk and Bayes action rule
items.statement: Posterior risk is the finite posterior integral of a jointly measurable nonnegative loss; a Bayes action rule is a measurable action map whose finite risk attains the minimum among finite-risk actions.
items.strategy: State measurability, finiteness, measurability of the selected rule, and attainment separately.

references.title: Andrew Gelman et al., Bayesian Data Analysis, 3rd ed., §9.1
Ryan Martin, Lecture Notes on Advanced Statistical Theory, §5.3.1, PDF pp. 104–105

items.title: The posterior mean uniquely minimizes squared posterior risk
items.statement: On fibers with finite posterior second moment, the measurable posterior-mean rule uniquely attains finite squared posterior risk; this result assumes AC through the L²-projection supplier.
items.strategy: Show the posterior mean is the conditional expectation on the trivial sigma-algebra and apply the supplied L² projection theorem.
items.axiom_use: Assume AC exactly for the published L² conditional-expectation projection theorem.

references.title: Ryan Martin, Lecture Notes on Advanced Statistical Theory, §5.3.1, PDF pp. 104–105
Andrew Gelman et al., Bayesian Data Analysis, 3rd ed., §9.1

items.title: Every posterior median minimizes absolute posterior risk
items.statement: With finite posterior first absolute moment, every posterior median minimizes absolute posterior risk; the measurable lower-median rule is an attained Bayes action rule.
items.strategy: Compare risks on the intervals separated by the median and use the two half-mass inequalities.

references.title: Ryan Martin, Lecture Notes on Advanced Statistical Theory, §5.3.1, PDF pp. 104–105
Alicia A. Johnson, Miles Q. Ott, and Mine Dogucu, Bayes Rules!, Chapter 8 §8.1

items.title: A maximal-mass action is Bayes under finite-class zero–one loss
items.statement: On a nonempty finite class, every posterior-mass maximizer minimizes zero–one posterior risk, and the least-indexed maximizer gives a measurable attained rule.
items.strategy: Compute the finite-class posterior risk and construct a measurable least-maximizer selector.

references.title: Ryan Martin, Lecture Notes on Advanced Statistical Theory, §5.3.1, PDF pp. 104–105
Andrew Gelman et al., Bayesian Data Analysis, 3rd ed., §9.1

title: Posterior prediction, credible sets, and Bayes actions — Examples

items.title: Posterior prediction adds parameter uncertainty to future sampling variation
items.statement: A two-point posterior mixed with Bernoulli future kernels has predictive mean one-half and variance one-quarter, entirely from posterior uncertainty.
items.strategy: Compute the mixed Bernoulli law and compare its variance with the two variance-decomposition terms.

references.title: Andrew Gelman et al., Bayesian Data Analysis, 3rd ed., §2.5
Alicia A. Johnson, Miles Q. Ott, and Mine Dogucu, Bayes Rules!, Chapter 8 §8.3

items.title: Asymmetric loss can change the posterior-optimal action
items.statement: With posterior mass 0.7 on class 1, false-positive cost 3, and false-negative cost 1, the zero–one action is class 1 but the asymmetric-loss action is class 0.
items.strategy: Calculate each finite posterior risk under each loss and compare the attained minima.

references.title: Andrew Gelman et al., Bayesian Data Analysis, 3rd ed., §9.1
Ryan Martin, Lecture Notes on Advanced Statistical Theory, §5.3.1, PDF pp. 104–105

items.title: A posterior median need not be unique
items.statement: For equal posterior mass on 0 and 1, every action in [0,1] is a median and has absolute posterior risk one-half.
items.strategy: Check the median inequalities and calculate the absolute-risk function on and outside the interval.

references.title: Ryan Martin, Lecture Notes on Advanced Statistical Theory, §5.3.1, PDF pp. 104–105
Alicia A. Johnson, Miles Q. Ott, and Mine Dogucu, Bayes Rules!, Chapter 8 §8.1

items.title: A continuous density mode need not distinguish zero–one actions
items.statement: A Beta(2,2) posterior has a unique density mode at one-half, yet exact zero–one posterior risk equals one for every point action.
items.strategy: Compute the density mode and use zero singleton mass to calculate every point-action risk.

references.title: Andrew Gelman et al., Bayesian Data Analysis, 3rd ed., §9.1
Ryan Martin, Lecture Notes on Advanced Statistical Theory, §5.3.1, PDF pp. 104–105

items.title: Posterior credibility does not ensure nominal frequentist coverage
items.statement: A central 95% credible interval under a uniform Beta prior and one Bernoulli observation has frequentist coverage zero at true parameter 0.005.
items.strategy: Derive both posterior intervals exactly and check that neither contains the chosen parameter value.

references.title: Andrew Gelman et al., Bayesian Data Analysis, 3rd ed., §2.5
Alicia A. Johnson, Miles Q. Ott, and Mine Dogucu, Bayes Rules!, Chapter 8 §8.1
